required: Prefer `npx wsdl-tsc pipeline` for full SOAP-to-REST adoption.
Use `pipeline` when the project needs a typed SOAP client, OpenAPI contract, REST gateway, and optional runnable app from the same WSDL.
Use `client`, `openapi`, `gateway`, `app`, or `compile` only when the task needs that narrower stage.
Use `compile` when the project needs to inspect WSDL compilation output or isolate generation problems.
Regenerate generated output from the WSDL source or `catalog.json` instead of editing generated files by hand.
Treat generated `client/`, `gateway/`, and `app/` output as replaceable artifacts.
Confirm the consumer project uses Node.js {{nodeMajor}} or newer.
Inspect the consumer project for WSDL files
ask only for the source location and the intended generation surface
Do not invent a service URL, input file, output path, or command scope.
Use this skill in a consumer project that depends on `@techspokes/typescript-wsdl-client`.
